gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-hk: Edo SZ draws every stroke like bent tubing, same gauge throughout. What stands out is that single gauge, which Noto Sans HK meets with big lowercase forms and brush ends lifted away before each curve closes.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-imperial-: Classic in feel, Edo SZ has no stress axis tilting its round letters. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic then loosens things, its c ends pointing apart like pincers and its capitals only a short step above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Edo SZ has the steadiness of a technical pen, with a lowercase that stands like cast iron capitals. Edo SZ makes the statement; Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian handles the reading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-jp: Laser-cut lines up top, one stroke width all the way, with Edo SZ standing tall like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans JP sweeps its curves open beneath, on a very tall x-height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Edo SZ has a blunt round-tip marker feel from end to end, built on one constant stroke width. Edo SZ takes the display; Noto Sans Kaithi's lowercase fills the line.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Cast-iron stature, zero shading: Edo SZ keeps every stroke constant, stem to arc, across its lowercase. Noto Sans Kannada's s curves, opening wide at both ends, then soften the whole page.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends away before each curve closes, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Noto Sans Kayah Li stays quiet so Edo SZ's pipe-like strokes carry the weight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels make Edo SZ unmistakable. Noto Sans Kharoshthi runs a thick, dark stripe of lowercase beneath, its curves never closing back on themselves.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean, its small letters standing proud. Edo SZ makes the statement with crossbars matching its stems, while Noto Sans Khmer does its best work through generous, chisel-notch openings.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Monoline construction gives Edo SZ a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Khojki, in turn, does its best work through a large, clear eye on every e.
